description: Physical-GPU validation matrix (#78). Each environment is one browser on one kind of device. Run validate.html there, download the validation bundle, commit it as bundlePath, then run `node tools/validation-summary.mjs --write` to update the README table. More environments can be added here (with a directory of the same name) from device reports.

record.how: From the user agent (Chrome: full version from client hints); check it against the browser's About page
Chrome: from client hints. Safari freezes the macOS version in the user agent: enter it from About This Mac
Mac: the model and chip from About This Mac, e.g. "MacBook Air 13-inch, M2". Windows and Linux: the machine and GPU, e.g. "Desktop, RTX 4070" or "ThinkPad X1, Iris Xe"
Detected: whether the adapter offers timestamp-query (GPU times) or only wall-clock times are available
Detected: whether the device was created with timestamp-query

environments.label: Apple silicon Mac · Chrome
environments.hardware: Mac with an Apple M-series chip
environments.notes: Current stable Chrome. Timestamps are quantized to about 100 µs unless chrome://flags/#enable-webgpu-developer-features is on; record which in the notes field.

environments.label: Apple silicon Mac · Safari (26 or later)
environments.hardware: Mac with an Apple M-series chip
environments.notes: Safari 26 or later with WebGPU on by default. timestamp-query may be missing: then every GPU time is wall-clock, which the bundle records.

environments.label: Windows PC, NVIDIA GPU · Chrome
environments.notes: Windows 10 or 11 with a recent NVIDIA driver. Laptop with two GPUs: say in the notes which one the browser used (adapter description).

environments.label: Windows PC, AMD GPU · Chrome
environments.notes: Windows 10 or 11 with a recent AMD driver; integrated Radeon or a discrete card (say which in the notes).

environments.label: Windows PC, Intel GPU · Chrome
environments.notes: Windows 10 or 11, Intel integrated (Iris Xe, Arc graphics) or a discrete Arc card.

environments.label: Windows PC · Firefox
environments.notes: Firefox 141 or later (WebGPU on by default on Windows). Note the GPU in the hardware field; timestamp-query may be missing.

environments.label: Linux, Vulkan · Chrome
environments.notes: Chrome on Linux with a Vulkan driver (Mesa or NVIDIA). If WebGPU is not on by default, say in the notes which flags were set (chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu and #enable-vulkan).
